title: ALMA Survey of Orion Planck Galactic Cold Clumps (ALMASOP): Deriving Inclination Angle and Velocity of the Protostellar Jets from Their SiO Knots
question: Can a shock-forming model of semi-periodical jet velocity variations derive the inclination angle and velocity of protostellar jets from single-epoch ALMA observations of SiO knots?

data.sensitivity: ~2.2 mJy beam^-1 (CO), ~2.0 mJy beam^-1 (SiO), ~2.7 mJy beam^-1 (C18O) per ~1.6 km s^-1 channel

what.value: Systemic velocities (V_sys) of the six targeted sources
SiO PV diagram measurements (Delta V_obs and V_obs) and CO outflow shell model parameters for G205S3 and G206

evidence.loc: SiO jets and the shock-forming model
evidence.quote: the values of $\Delta V_{\rm obs}$ and $V_{\rm obs}$ measured from the SiO PV diagrams (cite: 2022ApJ...925...11D),

evidence.loc: CO outflows and the wide-angle wind-driven shell model
evidence.quote: Note that the values for G205S3 and G206 are taken from (cite: 2022ApJ...925...11D).

what.value: SiO jet knot observations, proper motions, and radial velocities for HH 211

evidence.quote: In order to further test the shock-forming model, we applied it to three previously reported SiO jets, HH 211 (cite: 2016ApJ...816...32J; 2021ApJ...909...11J),

what.value: SiO and H2 jet knot observations, proper motions, and radial velocities for HH 212

evidence.quote: In the case of HH 212, we also included the H$_2$ knots in our analysis (cite: 2015ApJ...805..186L),

what.value: SiO jet knot observations, proper motions, and radial velocities for L1448C(N)

evidence.quote: and L1448C(N) (cite: 2021ApJ...906..112Y), of which the jet velocity and inclination angle have been derived independently from proper motion measurements and the observed radial velocity.

what.value: Mid-IR and sub-mm light curve variability classifications for protostars

evidence.loc: Jet Knot Timescales and Mid-IR/Sub-mm Light Curve Variability
evidence.quote: (cite: park21) analyzed 7-year mid-IR light curves of 735 protostars, classifying 140 (20%) as having dominant brightness variation timescales longer than three years.

evidence.loc: Jet Knot Timescales and Mid-IR/Sub-mm Light Curve Variability
evidence.quote: Similarly, (cite: lee21) classified 4-year sub-mm light curves of 43 protostars, and recovered 15 (35%) with dominant periods longer than three years.

recipe.goal: Determine systemic velocity of each target
recipe.method: Identify the velocity at the peak emission of the C18O position-velocity structure cut perpendicular to the jet axis through the source center
assumptions: Peak emission in C18O PV cut perpendicular to the jet axis represents the systemic velocity

recipe.goal: Measure SiO jet knot spatial and kinematic properties
recipe.method: Measure distance to first knot (D_obs) and average knot interval (Delta D_obs) from total intensity SiO maps, and measure radial sideways-ejection velocity (Delta V_obs) and radial jet velocity (V_obs) from SiO PV diagrams
key_parameters: Error on D_obs assumed to be -0.5 Delta D_obs and +0.5 beam size
assumptions: Knots very close to the central source (blueshifted side of G205S3, both sides of G206, BK0/RK0 in HH 211, R1-a/BI-a in L1448C(N)) have a different origin and are excluded; downstream knots are adopted as the first shock-formed knots

recipe.goal: Derive jet inclination angle, velocity, and velocity variation period using the shock-forming model
recipe.method: Apply analytical shock-forming model equations (Equations 3, 6, 7, 8) to measured D_obs, Delta D_obs, Delta V_obs, and V_obs to compute inclination angle i, jet velocity V_j, and period P
assumptions: Jet velocity varies sinusoidally with period P and amplitude Delta V: V = V_j - (Delta V / 2) sin(2 pi t / P)
No energy dissipation in shocks; thermal energy is totally transferred sideways so sideways-ejection velocity equals Delta V

recipe.goal: Fit CO outflow shells with the wide-angle wind-driven shell model
recipe.method: Fit projected parabolic shell equation (Eq. 11) to outflow boundaries in low-velocity CO channel maps and tilted parabolic PV equation (Eq. 12) to CO PV diagrams along the jet axis to obtain i, c, and t_0
assumptions: Outflow shell is a radially expanding parabolic shell with z = c R^2 and v_R = R / t_0

missing_for_reproduction: Adopted distances to the targets used to convert angular knot intervals (arcsec) and velocities (km s^-1) into periods P (years) in Table 1
Exact source coordinates and position angles for the PV cuts

Detailed fitting procedure (visual vs. numerical optimization) for the CO parabolic shell model in Equations 11 and 12
score_reason: The ALMA project code (2018.1.00302.S) is public, basic imaging parameters (CASA 5.4, tclean, robust 0.5, velocity resolution, beam, rms) are stated, and the analytical equations for both the shock-forming model and wind-driven shell model are fully given alongside all intermediate measured quantities in Table 1. However, calibration details, source coordinates, PV cut position angles, and target distances are delegated to companion ALMASOP papers.
rediscovery_reason: Public ALMA data (2018.1.00302.S) and a simple, explicit analytical recipe (Equations 1-12) with full intermediate and final numerical tables (Tables 1 and 2) make this a strong candidate for reproducing both the image-plane knot measurements and the derived kinematic parameters.
